text:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p95 latency spike detected on /v1/generate in us-east-1 (>800ms). AlertID: INC-2026-0317-01. Paging @oncall infra.

alice: seeing the same on dashboards, p50 ~120ms -> 200ms, p95 jumped to ~920ms at 15:07 UTC. Routing surface shows most requests hitting redwood-runtime-gpu-pool-a.

ben: confirmed. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/latency?svc=runtime&region=us-east-1. 15:02 stable, 15:07 spike. No error rate increase.

carla: grabbing logs from one affected host (rt-gpu-12). Grep for long tail spans:
```
2026-03-17T15:07:09Z request_id=... span_ms=780 route=/v1/generate node=rt-gpu-12
2026-03-17T15:07:12Z request_id=... span_ms=910 route=/v1/generate node=rt-gpu-12
```

carla: also seeing repeated epoll_wait wait events in host logs.

david: posting a quick perf sample from rt-gpu-12 (15:08):
```
# perf record --on-cpu top-like snapshot
samples: 1000
  40%  kernel/epoll_wait
  25%  python3  (syscall overhead)
  15%  softirq (sched)
```
Looks like syscalls/epoll is dominating.

infra-bot: Recent deploys in region: 15:00 kernel update rollout started (kernel-6.1.3 -> 6.1.4-custom) on 12 hosts, completed at 15:06.

alice: that kernel rollout timing lines up with the p95 jump. Hypothesis 1: kernel change introduced scheduler/epoll regression. Hypothesis 2: IO/batching change causing queueing at runtime. Need traces.

ben: I pulled a distributed trace for a slow request. Key span path:
```
client -> tcp_accept -> epoll_wait (90% time) -> read -> model_infer
```
epoll_wait long-blocking in kernel.

carla: can we get perf counters for softirq, ctx-switches around the window? I have `dmesg` from rt-gpu-12 showing increased softirqs.

carla: dmesg snippet:
```
[15:06:58] CPU0 softirq event: 34000
[15:07:05] CPU0 softirq event: 125000
```

ben: customer impact check: no 5xxs, but latency-sensitive customers likely affected. Notified CS to stand by.

eve: toggled extra replicaset (scale +20%) to absorb tail. Monitoring p95.

alice: mitigations to attempt: 1) Pause kernel rollout (stop remaining hosts). 2) Rollback kernel on a canary host (rt-gpu-12) to 6.1.3 and compare. 3) Temporarily route traffic away from rt-gpu-12.

david: running `sudo apt rollback kernel-6.1.3` on rt-gpu-12 now. Will report when reboot completes.

carla: collecting `perf stat -e context-switches,softirqs,cpu-clock` for 1 min on both pre/post hosts.

infra-bot: Revert signal: kernel rollout paused at 15:12 (4 hosts remaining).

ben: timeline so far (compact):
- 15:00 kernel rollout started (6.1.3 -> 6.1.4-custom)
- 15:06 rollout completed on 12 hosts
- 15:07 p95 jump detected (~920ms)
- 15:08 perf/trace shows epoll_wait dominating
- 15:12 rollback paused, canary rollback initiated

alice: update: rt-gpu-12 rebooted to 6.1.3 at 15:18. Early numbers: p95 on that node's local traffic down from 880ms -> 140ms.

ben: good signal — suggests kernel change is causal. But need to be careful: could be scheduler interaction with our runtime kernel config (epoll patch).

carla: attached logs for scope: `/var/log/redwood/runtime/rt-gpu-12/slow-requests.log` (snippet pasted here).

carla: logs also show batch flush times spiking around same window, weirdly. Maybe a timing interaction.

david: perf stat post-rollback (rt-gpu-12):
```
context-switches: 45k -> (before rollback 210k)
softirqs: 12k -> (before 98k)
cpu-time: consistent
```

ben: will open a ticket against our infra kernel config and cc kernel-vendor with trace and perf counters.

alice: on-call handoff: I'm handing to @ben for next 2 hours. Summary: p95 regression correlated with kernel rollout; rollback on canary resolved local p95; remaining work: validate across all hosts, vendor escalation, confirm no regression in other metrics.

ben: taking over. I'll coordinate rollout of rollback to remaining nodes in small batches, monitor p95, and file RCA. Adding action items: 1) block kernel-6.1.4-custom, 2) run regression test suite for epoll/syscall heavy workload, 3) prepare KB for future rollouts.

eve: adding incident label `severity-2` and notifying account teams.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status changed to "mitigated": partial rollback successful on canary, cluster scaling in effect.

ben: will keep thread updated with perf snapshots and traces. If p95 returns to baseline after rolling back remaining hosts, we mark root cause as kernel scheduling/epoll regression pending vendor fix.

alice: thanks team. please paste final timeline + artifacts into postmortems repo when done. :thumbsup:
